locator.text: Display 34.6, p. 34, in the proof of Lemma 4.7

evidence: paper: \|B^{-1}(d - \mathcal{Q}(c,c))\|_{C^j} \le r_j/2 + \nu_j q_j r_j^2 \le r_j, \qquad 2\nu_j q_j r_j \le \tfrac{1}{2}.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both inequalities are present, each inside the proof of one abstract Banach-space lemma, after a routine renaming and one substitution. Renaming: β ↔ ν_j (operator norm of B^{-1} = B.symm on the norm in play), K ↔ q_j (quadratic/bilinear norm of Q), r ↔ r_j, ‖·‖ ↔ ‖·‖_{C^j}. First chain: Lean's calc gives ‖B.symm (d - Q c)‖ ≤ β(‖d‖ + K r²) ≤ r; the paper's middle term r_j/2 + ν_j q_j r_j² is this term with β‖d‖ ≤ r/2 substituted, which is exactly hd : 2β‖d‖ ≤ r (an equality in the paper, where r_j := 2ν_j‖d‖_{C^j}). Second inequality: the paper's 2ν_j q_j r_j ≤ 1/2 is Lean's hcoef β * (K * (2 * r)) ≤ 1/2, derived from hsmall : 4βKr ≤ 1, which at r = 2ν‖d‖ is the paper's hypothesis 8ν_j² q_j ‖d‖_{C^j} ≤ 1 (and is spelled out in that form by ClosedIntervalMomentRepair.Data.Small and the calc at ClosedIntervalMomentRepair.lean:195-197). Two respects in which Lean is not narrower: Q is any map obeying the quadratic bounds rather than specifically c ↦ Q(c,c) bilinear, and r is any radius with 2β‖d‖ ≤ r rather than exactly 2ν‖d‖. Two respects in which it is packaged differently: the two inequalities sit in two separate lemmas rather than one display, and Lean fixes one norm on an abstract Banach space E, so the paper's j = 0,…,k family of C^j norms is obtained by instantiating per j (as ClosedIntervalMomentRepair does) rather than being quantified inside the lemma. No constant, exponent or sign differs.
